cells.tense: The direction you move in comes from what you feel, and you are not straining against it.
cells.ask: Add your own mark to one shared thing before you pass it on further.
cells.core:
The direction comes from how you feel about these people and practices, and the effort rides along with it instead of against it. You put something into the shared life you keep with others and it holds. Nothing in the motion is borrowed.

This is the version that survives a busy week and still feels like yours. The ask here is small and real. Add your own mark to one shared thing before you pass it on. The thing you hand over then carries a trace of you, not just what was already there. Keeping the rhythm takes one honest addition at a time, and this is a good week to make one.

cells.tense: You are racing toward a version where everyone finally gets it, and the pace is changing what you meant to protect.
cells.ask: Wait one cycle before adding the next piece, and let the quiet between you carry it.
cells.core:
You can feel when something shared needs defending, so you get there before anyone asks, and the meeting becomes a chance to steady it. The bracing is spending the very contact that made the practice worth keeping. You are guarding a room you have already stepped out of.

The offer is inside what the fear already knows. Wait one cycle before you add the next piece, and let the quiet between you carry it. Whatever passes back and forth is then theirs to hold, not yours to steer. Your direction is still there, and it does not need a hand on the wheel tonight. What you keep, you keep by letting it stand a moment on its own.

cells.tense: You know what this shared thing is for, and after a hard season you stopped putting your own direction into it.
cells.ask: Pick one small practice you already keep with someone, and tell them why it matters to you.
cells.core:
The feeling is still here. The moving is not. You tend what is shared by keeping your hands light on it, agreeable, not the one who says aloud what this is for. The direction has gone quiet in front of other people.

What is on offer is small. Pick one practice you already keep with someone, and tell them why it matters to you. Let them hear a reason in your own voice. The direction comes back by being used, not by being stored. One sentence is enough to start, and the sentence is yours. You are not missing the sense of what is worth carrying. You are missing the handing over of it.

cells.tense: You are already setting the direction for what these people keep, and you describe it as just how things are done.
cells.ask: Tell one person, in plain words, that you are the one carrying a practice they think runs itself.
cells.core:
The way you phrase things and what you let drop is steering what the group holds onto. It happens in the room, in front of you. But the credit goes to the practice itself, to the way it has been done, and you leave your own part out of the account.

The moving is running. Saying so has not. Tell one person, in plain words, that you are the one carrying a practice they think runs itself. You do not need a speech. The people you are with already feel the current. Staying unnamed costs you the right to count what you tend as yours, and that is a bill you pay every week.

attempts.check: The record supports a sense of direction that comes from feeling; it does not support the claim that this direction is visible to the person or that they can name where it came from, so any wording that implies a reportable history will overreach. A reader could reasonably say that they already know what settles them, so the Too Little and Unacknowledged cells must be about expression and placed credit, not about discovering a truth. The offers still hold if the read is wrong: each is a small, real action, not a proof. The sentence that most serves the writer is any claim that the merged feeling is a thing they can name on demand; I've kept the mechanism and left the naming out.
